They couldn't because of programming wildcards. Because 95 and 98 were so similar and supported essentially the exact same things, programmers/developers only had to differentiate those two from other versions like ME, XP, 2000, 3.1, etc.

So, to save money, time, memory, and efficiency in a sub-56K world, they only looked for "Win9*". Now, this "star" wildcard is special because it represents any number of characters, in any permutation, at any time. Thus:

9=91=97=9465356830=95=98

Because of this wildcard, any system identifying as "Win9" would undoubtedly identified as either Win95 or Win98.

So, short of having every programmer and developer go back and edit every line of code since 1994 to the present to assure that this wouldn't be a problem, Microsoft just skipped Win9 and went straight to a nice, even deca-number... 10.
